title: Symmetric and exterior algebras as quadratic duals
notes: The polynomial algebra has commutator relations and its dual is the Grassmann algebra; one displayed commutator uses mismatched indices.
statement: Over a field of characteristic different from two, the annihilator of the alternating relation space of \(S(V)\) is the symmetric relation space in \(V^*\otimes V^*\), giving \(S(V)^!=\bigwedge V^*\); dually \((\bigwedge V)^!=S(V^*)\). The exterior relations include the squares \(y_i^2=0\), as well as pairwise anticommutation. They cannot be omitted when merely writing the off-diagonal commutator pairing.
reconstruction: The displayed first product should be \(x_ix_k\), and diagonal relations are included. The characteristic restriction avoids a misleading symmetric-tensor shorthand in characteristic two.
fate: \citet[\S2.2(2)]{priddy1970koszul} records the polynomial/exterior dual cohomology calculation. The notebook is an elementary illustration of the preceding definition.

title: A quadratic hypersurface and its homogenized Clifford dual
notes: For \(A=S(V)/(\sum x_i^2)\), the orthogonal relation space consists of symmetric trace-zero matrices. The resulting relations are \(y_iy_j+y_jy_i=2\delta_{ij}h\), with \(h=y_i^2\) central.
statement: Let \(k\) have characteristic different from two and \(V\) have basis \(x_1,\ldots,x_d\). The quadratic dual of \(S(V)/(x_1^2+\cdots+x_d^2)\) has generators \(y_i\) of degree one, off-diagonal anticommutation, and equal squares. Equivalently it is the graded Clifford algebra with a central degree-two parameter \(h\) and relations \(y_iy_j+y_jy_i=2\delta_{ij}h\). Specializing \(h=1\) gives the usual Clifford algebra; \(h\) is not set to one in the graded dual.
reconstruction: The ground field and degree of \(h\) are specified; the summand \(a_{ij}x_ix_k\) is read as \(a_{ij}x_ix_j\).
fate: This is a direct example of the quadratic-dual definition in \citet[\S2]{beilinsonginzburgsoergel1996koszul}, already computed in the manuscript. No later new theorem is needed to settle it. The claim of centrality is part of the notebook calculation and follows from the equality of all squares.

title: The wonderful compactification of an adjoint symmetric space
notes: The space \(M=G/H\), with \(H\) a normalizer, has a minimal compactification \(\bar M\). The abbreviation for \(K\) is “compact subgroup”, and \(H/K\) is written as an elementary two-group.
statement: Let \(G\) be an adjoint semisimple complex algebraic group and \(\sigma\) an involution. For the appropriate normalizer of the connected fixed subgroup, the symmetric homogeneous space admits the De Concini--Procesi wonderful projective compactification. The construction uses an algebraic symmetric subgroup; a literal arbitrary compact subgroup of a complex group does not meet these hypotheses. Finite central isogenies and the choice between connected fixed subgroup, full fixed group, and its normalizer must be specified before asserting a quotient formula.
reconstruction: The algebraic symmetric-space hypotheses are reconstructed. The unqualified formula for \(H/K\) is not certified for arbitrary \(K\).
fate: \citet{deconciniprocesi1983complete}, published in 1983 from the 1982 Montecatini setting, is the original construction. Its exact adjoint-group setup is recalled in \citet[\S1]{chirivimaffei2004projective}. The notebook therefore presents established geometry; the isolated abbreviation does not determine an alternative real-form theorem.

title: Boundary divisors and the orbit stratification
notes: The compactification is smooth, has finitely many orbits, its boundary has normal crossings, and there is a unique closed orbit \(G/P\).
statement: For the preceding wonderful compactification of rank \(r\), the boundary consists of \(r\) smooth \(G\)-stable divisors meeting with simple normal crossings. Orbit closures are precisely their partial intersections, including the empty intersection \(X\); the total intersection is the unique closed orbit, a partial flag variety \(G/P\). At a point on exactly \(k\) boundary components, suitable local coordinates give their union by \(z_1\cdots z_k=0\), and their intersection by \(z_1=\cdots=z_k=0\). The codimension of the entire boundary is one, not \(k\).
reconstruction: The union/intersection distinction repairs the notebook parenthesis defining normal crossings.
fate: These are \citet[Theorem 3.1]{deconciniprocesi1983complete}, reproduced explicitly as \citet[Proposition 1.1]{chirivimaffei2004projective}. The latter primary text was read directly.

title: Restriction of line bundles to the closed orbit
notes: The last numbered property writes an isomorphism between line bundles on \(\bar M\) and those on \(G/P\).
statement: Restriction gives an injection \(\operatorname{Pic}(X)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Pic}(G/P)\); the image is a specified sublattice of the weight lattice. Surjectivity onto all line bundles of the closed orbit does not hold in general. The corrected assertion determines a line bundle on \(X\) uniquely by its restriction, without claiming that every line bundle on the closed orbit extends.

title: The finite Hecke algebra and its commuting generators
notes: The generators satisfy the quadratic and braid relations, with commuting condition \(j\ne i,i+1\).
statement: For \(q\ne0\), the type-A Hecke algebra has generators \(T_1,\ldots,T_{n-1}\), relations \((T_i+1)(T_i-q)=0\), the adjacent braid relation, and \(T_iT_j=T_jT_i\) for \(|i-j|>1\). It has basis \(T_w\) indexed by \(S_n\), and at \(q=1\) specializes to the symmetric-group algebra. The written condition incorrectly permits commuting with \(T_{i-1}\).
reconstruction: The generator normalization is explicitly matched rather than silently changing the quadratic relation.
fate: The finite type-A case is included in \citet[\S2]{mathas2004matrix}, whose generators use the alternate convention \(T_i\mapsto-T_i\). The notebook relation requires the absolute-distance condition.

title: Affine Hecke generators and the evaluation map
notes: Commuting lattice generators \(x_i\) are adjoined, with \(x_iT_i=T_ix_{i+1}-(q-1)x_{i+1}\). The proposed evaluation has \(x_n\mapsto1\), \(x_{n-1}\mapsto qT_{n-1}^2\).
statement: For the affine Hecke algebra of \(GL_n\), use commuting invertible \(X_i\), the finite Hecke generators, and the Bernstein relations. With the written convention they imply \(T_iX_iT_i=qX_{i+1}\), together with \(T_iX_j=X_jT_i\) for \(j\ne i,i+1\). Thus evaluation \(X_n=1\) recursively gives \(X_i=qT_i^{-1}X_{i+1}T_i^{-1}\), in particular \(X_{n-1}=qT_{n-1}^{-2}\). The displayed positive square is incompatible with the displayed exchange relation.

fate: The Jucys--Murphy elements in \citet[\S2]{mathas2004matrix} give the equivalent finite-algebra realization after reversing the indices and matching generator conventions. The inverse-square correction is an editorial consistency check of the notebook relations, not a new representation-theoretic theorem.

title: Polynomial quotients of the affine Hecke algebra
notes: Cherednik asks for the target algebra and homomorphism when \(x_n^2\mapsto1\), or more generally when a polynomial relation in \(x_n\) is imposed. The problem is marked unsolved.
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), let \(q\ne0\) and let \(p(z)=\prod_{a=1}^r(z-Q_a)\) be monic with every \(Q_a\ne0\). The quotient of the affine type-A Hecke algebra by the two-sided ideal generated by \(p(X_n)\) is a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type \(G(r,1,n)\), after reversing the affine convention. It has dimension \(r^n n!\), with a PBW basis of bounded powers of its commuting Murphy elements times \(T_w\). Repeated roots and nonsemisimple parameters do not invalidate this basis theorem. For \(r=2\) it is the type-B Hecke case, including \(p(z)=z^2-1\).
reconstruction: The polynomial is interpreted as a universal quotient relation, which gives a definite later solution to the question of its target. Nonzero roots match the invertible affine generators.
fate: \citet{arikikoike1994hecke} and the independent cyclotomic construction of Broue--Malle supplied this later answer. The exact presentation and Ariki--Koike basis theorem are read in \citet[\S2, (2.2)]{mathas2004matrix}, first circulated in August 2001 and published in 2004. This identifies the universal quotient; it does not claim that every such quotient admits an evaluation back into the original \(n!\)-dimensional finite Hecke algebra.
present_status: As of 12 November 2026, the universal polynomial-quotient problem is settled by cyclotomic Hecke algebras and their basis theorem. No generic semisimplicity assumption is needed for this answer.
